text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The draft budget for 1998 increases funding of the interior ministry by 25 percent or 149 million kroons and permits it to sign lease agreements worth 240 million kroons.
- The mayor of Tallinn calls for a special statute for the central Town Hall Square in order to better regulate the activities of open-air beer gardens there.
- The Estonia concert hall will open again today after two-month repair works.
- The police have appealed to the press council to take measures against two commercial radio stations broadcasting traffic information, including the location and activities of police patrols.
- The incompetent performance of Baltic social ministers' at a Nordic-Baltic seminar on sex equality in Latvia made Nordic politicians say the three countries are fit for EU entry.
- Austrian Airlines/Lauda Air will open a Vienna-Tallinn air route from October 26. There will be three flights per week.
- Colonel Ants Laaneots, chief of the general staff, explained to the daily the operations of the planned Baltic Defence College to be founded in Tartu.
- Banks say that the demand for housing loans continues to be high and will last at least until the end of the year.
- Hansa Leasing, a subsidiary of Hansapank, signed a loan agreement with 10 European banks in Riga for 50 million marks.
- A 14-story business centre will be built in central Tartu by the end of 1998.
